_note: Pseudocode is condensed from RFC 8986 / RFC 9800. Vendor support is indicative; check docs/implementations for versions.

behaviors.name: End
behaviors.summary: Plain endpoint: advance to the next segment and forward on the IPv6 FIB.
behaviors.definition: The SID is a node SID. The node updates the IPv6 DA to the next SID in the SRH and forwards the packet using a regular IPv6 FIB lookup. Flavors (PSP, USP, USD) from RFC 8986 modify SRH handling at the penultimate/ultimate hop.
pseudocode: S01. If (Segments Left == 0) -> stop SRH processing, process next header
S02. If (Hop Limit <= 1) -> ICMP Time Exceeded (code 0), discard
S03. If (Last Entry > max_LE or Segments Left > Last Entry+1) -> ICMP Parameter Problem, discard
S04. Decrement Hop Limit; decrement Segments Left
S05. DA = SegmentList[Segments Left]
S06. Lookup DA in the IPv6 FIB and forward
use_cases: Node steering in a segment list

behaviors.name: End.X
behaviors.summary: Endpoint with cross-connect to a specific layer-3 adjacency.
behaviors.definition: Like End, but instead of an FIB lookup the packet is forwarded out a specific layer-3 adjacency (interface plus next hop). Equivalent to an adjacency SID.
pseudocode: S01. If (Segments Left == 0) -> stop SRH processing, process next header
S02. If (Hop Limit <= 1) -> ICMP Time Exceeded (code 0), discard
S03. If (Last Entry > max_LE or Segments Left > Last Entry+1) -> ICMP Parameter Problem, discard
S04. Decrement Hop Limit; decrement Segments Left
S05. DA = SegmentList[Segments Left]
S06. Forward the packet to the L3 adjacency J bound to this SID (no FIB lookup)

behaviors.name: End.T
behaviors.summary: Endpoint with specific IPv6 table lookup.
behaviors.definition: Like End, but the next-hop lookup is performed in a specific IPv6 table T instead of the default FIB.
pseudocode: S01. If (Segments Left == 0) -> stop SRH processing, process next header
S02. If (Hop Limit <= 1) -> ICMP Time Exceeded (code 0), discard
S03. If (Last Entry > max_LE or Segments Left > Last Entry+1) -> ICMP Parameter Problem, discard
S04. Decrement Hop Limit; decrement Segments Left
S05. DA = SegmentList[Segments Left]
S06. Lookup DA in IPv6 table T and forward

behaviors.name: End.DX6
behaviors.summary: Decapsulate and cross-connect to a layer-3 IPv6 adjacency.
behaviors.definition: Terminates the SRv6 tunnel: removes the outer IPv6 header (with SRH) and forwards the inner IPv6 packet to a specific layer-3 adjacency. Used for per-CE VPN SIDs.
pseudocode: S01. If (Next Header != SRH or Segments Left == 0) -> proceed; else discard (ICMP Parameter Problem)
S02. If (Upper-layer header type == 41 IPv6) -> pop the outer IPv6 header and its extension headers
S03. Forward the resulting packet to L3 adjacency J (no FIB lookup)
S04. Else discard

behaviors.name: End.DX4
behaviors.summary: Decapsulate and cross-connect to a layer-3 IPv4 adjacency.
behaviors.definition: Same as End.DX6 but the inner packet is IPv4 and is forwarded to an IPv4 adjacency.
pseudocode: S01. If (Next Header != SRH or Segments Left == 0) -> proceed; else discard (ICMP Parameter Problem)
S02. If (Upper-layer header type == 4 IPv4) -> pop the outer IPv6 header and its extension headers
S03. Forward the resulting IPv4 packet via IPv4 adjacency J
S04. Else discard
use_cases: IPv4 CE attachment over an IPv6 core

behaviors.name: End.DT6
behaviors.summary: Decapsulate and specific IPv6 table lookup.
behaviors.definition: Terminates the tunnel and looks up the inner IPv6 destination in a specific IPv6 table (typically a VRF). The common per-VRF SID for IPv6 L3VPN.
pseudocode: S01. If (Next Header != SRH or Segments Left == 0) -> proceed; else discard (ICMP Parameter Problem)
S02. If (Upper-layer header type == 41 IPv6) -> pop the outer IPv6 header and its extension headers
S03. Set the packet's associated FIB table to T
S04. Lookup the inner destination in table T and forward
S05. Else discard

behaviors.name: End.DT4
behaviors.summary: Decapsulate and specific IPv4 table lookup.
behaviors.definition: Terminates the tunnel and looks up the inner IPv4 destination in a specific IPv4 table (typically a VRF). The common per-VRF SID for IPv4 L3VPN.
pseudocode: S01. If (Next Header != SRH or Segments Left == 0) -> proceed; else discard (ICMP Parameter Problem)
S02. If (Upper-layer header type == 4 IPv4) -> pop the outer IPv6 header and its extension headers
S03. Set the packet's associated FIB table to T
S04. Lookup the inner destination in IPv4 table T and forward
S05. Else discard

behaviors.name: End.B6.Encaps
behaviors.summary: Endpoint bound to an SR Policy, with encapsulation.
behaviors.definition: A Binding SID. When the packet arrives, the node advances the segment list, then encapsulates the packet in a new outer IPv6 header carrying the SRH of the bound SR policy and forwards it. Hides the policy's segment list from upstream nodes.
pseudocode: S01. If (Segments Left == 0) -> discard (ICMP Parameter Problem)
S02. If (Hop Limit <= 1) -> ICMP Time Exceeded, discard
S03. Decrement Hop Limit; decrement Segments Left; DA = SegmentList[Segments Left]
S04. Push a new outer IPv6 header with SRH containing the bound SR Policy's segment list
S05. Set outer Source Address = this node; outer DA = first SID of the policy
S06. Lookup outer DA in the FIB and forward
use_cases: Hiding long segment lists / reducing SRH size (MSD limits)

behaviors.name: End.B6.Encaps.Red
behaviors.summary: End.B6.Encaps with a reduced SRH (first SID carried only in the DA).
behaviors.definition: Same as End.B6.Encaps, but the first SID of the policy is placed only in the outer DA and omitted from the new SRH, saving 16 bytes.
pseudocode: S01-S03. As End.B6.Encaps
S04. Push a new outer IPv6 header with a reduced SRH (policy segment list minus its first SID)
S05. Outer DA = first SID of the policy
S06. Lookup outer DA in the FIB and forward
use_cases: Same as End.B6.Encaps where header overhead matters (MTU, ASIC parsing depth)

behaviors.name: H.Encaps
behaviors.summary: SR headend with encapsulation in an SR policy.
behaviors.definition: Headend behavior: the ingress node steers a packet into an SR policy by pushing an outer IPv6 header and an SRH containing the full segment list.
pseudocode: S01. Push an outer IPv6 header with SRH containing the SR Policy segment list
S02. Outer Source Address = encapsulating node address; outer DA = first SID
S03. Set Next Header per payload (IPv4/IPv6/Ethernet); Hop Limit per policy
S04. Lookup outer DA in the FIB and forward
use_cases: Steering traffic into SR policies (BGP color, ODN, static)

behaviors.name: H.Encaps.Red
behaviors.definition: Same as H.Encaps but the first SID is carried only in the outer DA, so the SRH holds one fewer entry. With a single-SID policy the SRH can be omitted entirely.
pseudocode: S01. Push an outer IPv6 header; first SID goes to the outer DA only
S02. If the policy has more than one SID, add an SRH with the remaining SIDs
S03. Lookup outer DA in the FIB and forward
use_cases: Default for most L3VPN deployments to minimize overhead
Short segment lists with no SRH

behaviors.name: uN
behaviors.summary: Compressed node SID: shift the next micro-SID into the active position.
behaviors.definition: uN is the NEXT-C-SID flavor of End. A uSID carrier (an IPv6 address) holds a locator block followed by several 16-bit micro-SIDs. The node matching the first uSID shifts the remaining uSIDs left and forwards; no SRH is needed for short paths.
pseudocode: S01. DA = [Block | active uSID | uSID2 | uSID3 | ... | 0]
S02. If (Hop Limit <= 1) -> ICMP Time Exceeded, discard
S03. If (remaining uSIDs after the active one are all zero) -> behave as classic End (use SRH if present)
S04. Else DA = [Block | uSID2 | uSID3 | ... | 0 | 0]   (shift left by one uSID, pad with zeros)
S05. Decrement Hop Limit; lookup new DA in the FIB and forward
use_cases: Compressed SR paths in a single 128-bit carrier (up to ~6 uSIDs for F3216)
Data center and WAN uSID deployments
Reducing header overhead versus classic SRH

behaviors.name: uA
behaviors.summary: Compressed adjacency SID: shift and forward over a specific adjacency.
behaviors.definition: uA is the NEXT-C-SID flavor of End.X: it shifts the uSID carrier like uN but forwards over a specific layer-3 adjacency instead of an FIB lookup.
pseudocode: S01. Same shift logic as uN (S02-S04)
S02. Forward the packet to the L3 adjacency bound to the uA uSID (no FIB lookup)

behaviors.name: uDT4
behaviors.definition: The terminating uSID for IPv4 L3VPN. As the last uSID in the carrier it is processed like End.DT4: decapsulate and look up the inner IPv4 packet in the VRF table.
pseudocode: S01. DA matches [Block | Node | uDT4 function]; no further uSIDs follow
S02. Pop the outer IPv6 header (and SRH if present)
S03. Lookup the inner IPv4 destination in VRF table T and forward
use_cases: IPv4 L3VPN service SID advertised via BGP with uSID

behaviors.name: uDT6
behaviors.definition: Same as uDT4 for IPv6: terminating uSID that decapsulates and looks up the inner IPv6 packet in a VRF table.
pseudocode: S01. DA matches [Block | Node | uDT6 function]; no further uSIDs follow
S02. Pop the outer IPv6 header (and SRH if present)
S03. Lookup the inner IPv6 destination in VRF table T and forward
use_cases: IPv6 L3VPN service SID with uSID
Global-table or VRF decap in compressed networks
